subject: math
cluster: Visualize relationships between two-dimensional and three-dimensional objects
intro: A cross section is the 2D shape you get when a plane slices through a 3D solid. For example, slicing a cylinder horizontally gives a circle; slicing it vertically gives a rectangle. Slicing a sphere in any direction gives a circle. Rotating a 2D shape about a line (an axis) sweeps out a 3D solid: rotating a rectangle about one side gives a cylinder; rotating a right triangle about a leg gives a cone; rotating a semicircle about its diameter gives a sphere.

items.prompt: What cross section results from slicing a cylinder parallel to its base?

steps: A horizontal slice of a cylinder is parallel to its circular base.
That slice has the same shape as the base.
So the cross section is a circle.

items.prompt: What 3D solid is formed by rotating a right triangle about one of its legs?

steps: Rotating the triangle sweeps out a solid of revolution.
A right triangle spun about a leg traces a cone.
So the solid is a cone.

items.prompt: What solid is formed by rotating a rectangle about one of its sides?

steps: Rotating the rectangle sweeps a solid.
A rectangle spun about a side traces a cylinder.
So the solid is a cylinder.
It is the shape from slicing a solid with a plane.
solution.answer: The 2D shape formed when a plane slices a 3D solid.

items.prompt: What cross section does any slice of a sphere give?

steps: A sphere slices to the same shape in every direction.

items.prompt: Rotating a semicircle about its diameter gives what solid?
